source.author: verg
source.text: Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_original: 'Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis / lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra / spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_english: First, within the heavens, the lands, the watery plains, the shining orb of the Moon, and the Titanian stars, a spirit nourishes all things from within; poured through its limbs, mind stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quidam nostrorum hunc esse aiunt spiritum, quo omnis mundus inspiratur et regitur; et cuncta habent notitiam Dei, quem juxta Stoicos insignis poeta scribens, ait: Principio coelum ac terras camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque astra Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus, Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_original: Quidam nostrorum hunc esse aiunt spiritum, quo omnis mundus inspiratur et regitur; et cuncta habent notitiam Dei, quem juxta Stoicos insignis poeta scribens, ait: Principio coelum ac terras camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque astra Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus, Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_english: Some of our people say that this is the spirit by which the whole world is breathed into and governed; and that all things have knowledge of God, whom, in accordance with the Stoics, a distinguished poet, writing, says: In the first place, heaven and earth and the watery plains, and the shining orb of the moon, and Titan’s stars, the Spirit within nourishes: and, poured through the limbs, Mind stirs the whole mass, and mingles itself with the great body.
